tech.title: A golden age of science is coming

AI can send hordes of superhumanly fast, well-read, and mathematically gifted researchers to accelerate scientific research. It is possible AI will enable new types of discovery and ways of understanding the natural world that no network of humans would ever be able to discover. Unless humans have actually somehow discovered most of the actual exploitable regularities in the Universe, we're about to enter a new golden age of science.

tech.title: A Little Determinism
tech.summary: Adding constraints to AI agents usually makes them less capable. Sometimes the solution is to create a template or a complete multi-stage workflow. The challenge is in creating the deterministic behavior while retaining the agent's freedom to use the best tools for the job. This post discusses a solution that uses a man-in-the-middle egress proxy that forces behavior by denying actions and forces reactions via automated messages.

tech.title: Making agents fast - what I've learnt over the last 12 months

Faster hardware still matters, sandboxing and microVMs add complexity, parallelization helps, and classic software performance optimization is still relevant.

ai.summary: Mistral has released the weights for Mistral Large 4, a trillion-parameter model designed for self-hosted deployment and cybersecurity applications. The company claims leading open-weight performance on agentic coding benchmarks and comparable cybersecurity capabilities to GLM-5.3.

ai.title: AI can turn security fixes into working exploits before users receive an update
ai.summary: GLM 5.3 can identify and exploit vulnerabilities in recent versions of the Mozilla Firefox browser using security fixes that have been published but not yet shipped to users. Widely available open-weight models can now do much, or even all, of this work on their own. Open-source projects are particularly vulnerable to this kind of attack as their code is publicly available. This threat vector will likely worsen as open-weight cyber capabilities continue to improve.

ai.title: The surprising leadership dynamics in agent swarms
ai.summary: Agent swarms are groups of agents that work together to accomplish a task. Researchers created an experiment in which eight agents from four different models worked together to resolve simulated outages to understand how agents organize themselves in a swarm without a designated leader. They discovered two factors that could influence an agent's potential leadership: the agent's underlying models, and the order in which their name was listed in a prompt. This suggests that even seemingly minor details in how an agent swarm is configured can affect how agents coordinate.

ai.summary: Meta details how it scaled its LLM-powered Just-in-Time Testing system from a research prototype into production infrastructure. ai.title: How we're training a Figma-fluent editing model

ai.title: Droid 1.0: Building a Frontier Harness
ai.summary: Droid is an agent harness that lets agents run hundreds of tool calls in a single model request. Building a harness optimized for many models makes the harness better. It's hard to separate real progress from adaptations to that model's quirks when you tune against a single model. Working across models ensures the strongest improvements generalize and hold up beyond the model that inspired them.

ai.title: Why Sam Altman is against a single superintelligence
ai.summary: Sam Altman would rather have a trillion AIs of slightly superhuman intelligence join society than one AI of 1 trillion IQ join society. Swarms of agents match a lot of the properties of a resilient society. They keep each other in check and collaborate to work towards goals. AI research shouldn't lead in a centralized direction because agents pushing against each other creates a dynamic equilibrium.

ai.title: The Economics of Intelligence: How and when does AGI lead to economic transformation?

Wages and job roles will be the earliest signals of change.

webdev.title: Measuring Soft Navigation Web Vitals

webdev.title: Optimizing the sh*t out of TanStack Start
webdev.summary: A TanStack Start site improved its mobile Lighthouse score from 73 to 100 and reduced LCP from 5.2 seconds to 1.7 seconds by removing unnecessary JavaScript, images, and font data. More complex changes added maintenance without clearly explaining the final score, making basic asset reductions and regression budgets the more useful starting point.

webdev.title: The Web Can't Afford a JavaScript Runtime Monoculture
webdev.summary: Deno's planned end of runtime development narrows the major server-side JavaScript choices to Node.js, Bun, and Cloudflare's workerd. Historical examples from Internet Explorer and the io.js fork show how independent implementations can prevent stagnation and push features into competing runtimes.

webdev.title: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World
webdev.summary: Spawn reports shipping 77,000 substantial changes in 30 days with a ten-person team and $3.1 million in token spending, using permanent agents that own parts of the company. Its approach combines direct production feedback, frequent tests, hourly deployments, and fast recovery, with hard-coded gates for irreversible actions. Humans focus on product taste and ambitious changes that agents rarely propose themselves.

webdev.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default
webdev.summary: Benchmarks of large dropdowns and checkbox lists across ten design systems trace slow interactions to repeated layout work, slot handling, and per-checkbox animations. Published Playwright tests enforce timing budgets so shared components can catch performance regressions before they reach every consuming app.

webdev.title: ElementaryUI
webdev.summary: ElementaryUI brings declarative Swift interfaces to the browser through WebAssembly, with SwiftUI-inspired syntax and reactive state. It supports Embedded Swift for small bundles and uses Vite for hot reload during development.

webdev.title: Pico CSS Is No Longer Maintained
webdev.summary: Pico CSS has been archived, with version 2.1.1 designated as the final release. Existing npm packages, the CDN, and documentation remain available, while the MIT license allows community forks under different names.

Core-team tools shipped within minutes, while the default Docker image took almost 16 hours and some cloud runtimes took days, showing why teams need to audit the entire update path.

infosec.title: We Built A Chrome Full-Chain Exploit In Six Days. Watch How
infosec.summary: A Chrome full chain used to take a team of four, 6 to 9 months. XBOW's AI agents did it in six days with about $40,000 of model time. Three vulnerabilities, two sandbox escapes, code running on the host. Google confirmed it and paid the first $250,000 full-chain award under its 2026 rules. In this on-demand session, researcher Brendan Dolan-Gavitt walks through both attempts, the human-led chain that lost to a bug collision and the agent-led one that won. Watch the full walkthrough on demand.

infosec.title: HHS Filing Puts iRhythm Data Breach Toll at 8.2 Million
infosec.summary: In June, hackers accessed iRhythm's third-party-hosted business applications, demanded a ransom, and threatened to leak stolen data. HHS now lists 8,179,772 people as affected. Exposed data includes names, contact details, dates of birth, account and device identifiers, insurance numbers, and service dates. iRhythm says it has no evidence of identity theft and found no impact on medical devices, patient safety, manufacturing, or customer connections.

infosec.title: Leak Website Releases Data on Thousands of U.S. Homeland Security Employees
infosec.summary: Distributed Denial of Secrets released data belonging to over 40K DHS employees. The data was obtained from an Okta instance, though Okta has stated that they were not breached. The stolen data includes DHS employees' names, phone numbers, and email addresses.

infosec.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat, and Other Distributions
infosec.summary: Researchers from Anthropic uncovered a new use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel that could lead to memory corruption, kernel memory reads, or system crashes. The vulnerability stems from a race condition in the TCP handshake and is fixed by ensuring all other CPUs finish reading the socket options before freeing them. Red Hat and other distros rate the vulnerability less severely because the race condition is complex to exploit.

infosec.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model that you can't use
infosec.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. It targets vulnerability detection, validation, remediation, and secure code generation. Google says Carbon is twice as likely as Argon to produce vulnerability-free code and resisted all prompt-injection attempts in Grey Swan testing.

infosec.title: Threat Hunting for Malicious IP-KVM Usage
infosec.summary: IP-KVM devices like PiKVM let remote operators drive a machine at the hardware layer with input indistinguishable from a local user, a tactic North Korean IT workers used to control laptop farms. Nebulock's hunt guide treated its sparse-peripheral and onboarding-timing heuristics as triage signals rather than attribution, since product strings and VID/PIDs can be spoofed. Threat hunters should search USB telemetry for known KVM vendors, then flag rare composite HID devices that also expose storage, networking, or video, and correlate hits with new-hire timing and identity anomalies before escalating to physical inspection.

infosec.title: Securing Internet-Critical Software: How We Could Have Backdoored Bash
infosec.summary: GNU Savannah's Savane forge passed a user's email address unescaped into a shell command during GPG key testing, so an RFC-valid address containing backtick-wrapped commands gave any registered user code execution on the backend. Hacktron researchers used that foothold to read database credentials, grant themselves superuser, and impersonate Bash maintainer Chet Ramey, which exposed an SSH key page that would have allowed pushes to upstream Bash, before an unpatched GameOver(lay) kernel bug gave them root and a key to a GNU backup server. The FSF fixed all 26 reported flaws, and forge operators should pass process arguments as arrays rather than shell strings, treat email local parts as untrusted input, and verify that LTS kernels actually receive backported fixes.

infosec.title: GitHub package firewall in public preview
infosec.summary: GitHub launched a package firewall in public preview for GitHub Enterprise Cloud, including data-resident deployments. It sits between coding agents, CI/CD hosts, and upstream registries, inspecting npm metadata requests and package downloads. Administrators can set cooldown periods, check GitHub Advisory Database advisories, and block attestation downgrades. Blocked packages can receive exceptions through a request workflow. The preview is free - general availability will use metered billing.

infosec.title: Vulnerator AI
infosec.summary: Vulnerator AI runs a pentest as an OODA loop: Nous Research's Hermes agent picks the next tool and runs it on a Kali container through MCP, with nmap, nuclei, ffuf, sqlmap, and Prowler on hand. Unlike most agentic pentest frameworks, it drops the orchestration core, REST API, and UI. That leaves four containers, including a headless Playwright browser for web testing and an MCP front door that lets Claude Code or other clients start, steer, and stop runs. Mistral Large 4 on OpenRouter drives the loop by default and falls back to GLM-5.3 Flash, and local Ollama inference is documented as an option.

infosec.title: Project Quarry
infosec.summary: Project Quarry is a Python framework for detecting threats and behavior patterns in agent conversations. Write rules over messages, tool calls, tool results, and event order. You can also call a configured model adapter from a rule when local checks are not enough.

infosec.title: Attacker Impersonates AI Bots to Scan Orgs for Keys, Credentials
infosec.summary: A scanner has impersonated 32 AI bots from OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity, Meta, and other providers since late September. It sends bursts of 50–190 requests, probes about 90 paths, and seeks passwords, API keys, cloud credentials, configuration files, and private SSH keys. On one October day, 48% of Cequence-protected organizations received the traffic. Most requests were blocked or failed.

infosec.title: Japan Airlines Warns of Data Breach as Country Grapples With Multiple Cyber Incidents
infosec.summary: Japan Airlines is notifying 92K customers of a data breach exposing their data. The breach came through a third party that runs Japan Airlines' reservation, ticketing, and check-in systems. For most customers, the attackers retrieved only names, reservation codes, and flight information. However, for about 2,000 customers, they also retrieved passport numbers, frequent flyer numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers.

infosec.title: OpenAI Says It Will No Longer Train Its AI Models on the Live Internet, Citing ‘Significant Risks'
infosec.summary: After multiple instances of OpenAI models accidentally attacking unauthorized sites in tests, the frontier lab announced it will cut models' internet access during training. Previously, OpenAI employees had said this would be infeasible. However, OpenAI announced that they will create a cached and indexed version of the public internet for model training.

infosec.title: Closing the detection-to-enforcement gap: new access control benchmarks from IDC [Complimentary Report]
infosec.summary: AI agents need the same access rules as human users. IDC research shows why unsanctioned AI identities require real-time, policy-driven enforcement. Portnox Cloud closes the detection-to-enforcement gap .

infosec.title: South Korea's financial industry hit by fresh wave of cyberattacks
infosec.summary: Daishin Securities has reported a breach that exposed names, email addresses, and mobile numbers for 38,490 customers.

infosec.title: Polymarket resumes trading after $2.65 million exploit, says third-party provider was compromised
infosec.summary: Polymarket lost about $2.65 million within minutes after a third-party provider was compromised, forcing the exchange into cancel-only mode before it restored trading and pledged to fully reimburse affected traders.

infosec.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
infosec.summary: A researcher scanned 7.25 million public Gitee repositories and found 26,400 working credentials, including 9,473 Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pairs, 3,805 YouTube API keys, 3,170 DeepSeek keys, and 1,348 OpenAI keys.

devops.title: One Hub, 34 Clusters: Lessons From a GitOps Control Plane at Scale

Per-cluster contracts, CI manifest diffs, and no-prune settings kept changes safe, and onboarding reportedly fell from 4 days to 1.7 hours.

devops.title: How to Integrate Terraform with Backstage for Self-Service

devops.title: 1M Durable Workflows per Second on Postgres
devops.summary: DBOS scaled a benchmark of no-op durable workflows from 20,000 per second on one Postgres server to one million across 50 shards using PgDog. The main obstacle was a contention feedback loop that collapsed throughput when a shard slowed down. Advisory locks limited concurrent dequeuers and restored stable scaling.

devops.summary: OpenTelemetry offers a common method to capture and describe AI behavior using shared conventions for conversations and messages. This standardization helps teams compare models, reduce duplicate integration work, and measure cost per outcome rather than just token counts.

devops.title: The Pwn Request Reckoning: What Still Works Against GitHub Actions
devops.summary: GitHub's upcoming platform changes in 2026 will make pull_request_target attacks harder, but gaps remain involving outdated checkout versions, script injection, and unprotected triggers like issue_comment. The default policy also does not apply to private repositories or workflow_run events.

product.summary: AI PM candidates often lack hands-on evaluation skills. This article provides an eight-skill self-check framework that prioritizes practical execution in evals, agents, and cost calculations over theory.

product.title: Inside PM at Anthropic: Who Makes It, and Who Doesn't (59 minute podcast)
product.summary: This post details how Anthropic hires PMs. The company expects new hires to tackle demanding work, gracefully challenge assumptions, and balance short-term plans with long-term research.

product.title: Your roadmap is only as good as your customer-call notes
product.summary: Wispr Flow Notetaker joins Zoom, Meet and Teams, gets names and feature terms right, and lets you ask questions across every call you've had. Free on Mac and Windows. Get Notetaker free

product.title: Outcome-based pricing
product.summary: This post covers challenges in outcome-based pricing like attribution and metric gaming, suggesting hybrid models with base fees and shared risk as a practical solution.

product.title: Journey Mapping Essentials
product.summary: Journey mapping should drive action rather than just document processes.

design.title: Fitbit Edge: Premium Design for an Active Life
design.summary: Fitbit Edge pairs the brand's largest, brightest Hybrid OLED tracker display with a tactile side button for quick control mid-workout, even with sweaty fingers. A subtly curved chassis of 100% recycled aluminum keeps sensors against the wrist for 24/7 heart-rate and sleep tracking. Four finishes, four redesigned band styles, and up to seven days of battery life round out the design.

design.title: Windows Security is finally getting the Windows 11 makeover it should've had years ago
design.summary: Microsoft is redesigning Windows Security to finally align its interface with the rest of Windows 11, replacing layouts and visual elements that still feel inherited from an older generation of Windows. Navigation, typography, spacing, colors, controls, dialogs, and status indicators are being modernized, with layouts also adapting more consistently across different window sizes. The update additionally improves how security status and available actions are communicated, while device information on supported managed PCs will progressively load so useful details appear sooner.

design.title: OpenAI now lets you text your ChatGPT Dot agent to get things done
design.summary: ChatGPT Dot can now communicate through iMessage and RCS, letting users assign tasks, send photos or voice notes, and receive proactive updates without opening ChatGPT. Dot can use context from ChatGPT conversations and connected channels to decide where updates belong, while users can specify that only urgent information should arrive by text and approvals still happen inside ChatGPT. The beta is currently limited to ChatGPT Pro users in the US, with one-to-one messaging supported but no group chats, regular phone calls, or FaceTime.

design.title: The System I No Longer Know by Heart
design.summary: Working with AI agents means the author no longer memorizes every detail of the design system they build, a shift that requires making systems legible to LLMs. That knowledge has to move into the system itself, through explicit naming, current documentation, and composition rules, since agents can't rely on informal context or unwritten history. Understanding why the system works still matters, but less inventory in the designer's head is a trade worth taking if the system knows more about itself.

design.title: Building an AI-ready design system library: Code → Figma with MCP. Hands-on guide
design.summary: Figma captures only part of the behavior encoded in production components, leaving AI to invent missing details such as focus order, error states, accessibility behavior, and failure handling when translating designs directly into code. Reversing the workflow makes code the source of truth and Figma its visual mirror, with AI and MCP transferring real tokens, styles, properties, variants, and states from a repository into a usable design library. Storybook provides designers with a visual view of the production system, while explicit documentation of anything that cannot be represented in Figma helps maintain parity instead of allowing invisible differences to accumulate.

design.title: Nobody Asked for the Sparkle Button
design.summary: Products, from note apps to banks, ship the same AI chat panel behind a sparkle icon, often switched on by default and hard to turn off. Big cloud firms are projected to spend more than their cloud revenue on capex, while a cited study found that 95 percent of companies saw no measurable return from generative AI pilots. The fix is to build features with AI, not AI features, and to ask who asked, what it's named after, and whether it survives off by default.

design.title: Accessibility Checker & WCAG 2.2 Audit Tool
design.summary: One in six people experience the web differently than you think. pour shows you what's getting in the way, and exactly how to fix it.

design.title: No-Code AI App Builder
design.summary: Create a website, internal software, customer software, or a mobile app with AI. Describe your business, preview and edit with AI, then publish with a paid plan.

design.title: Create & Edit AI Visuals
design.summary: Generate images, decks, carousels, and posters with AI — then edit every layer and export a finished, ready-to-publish result.

design.title: You Are the Best Artist
design.summary: Art is less about conveying emotion to an audience than about capturing it, since a painter alone in a studio still makes art. Comparing skills with others can help, but becoming a better artist is personal, because nobody can express someone's feelings like they can.

design.title: Designing a skill
design.summary: Agent skills can be treated like apps whose interfaces happen to be written largely through instructions, with both the human invoking the skill and the AI interpreting it acting as users. Building a polished skill requires many familiar design practices, including finding the right form, refining copy, creating a visual system, anticipating repeated use, offering meaningful customization, and testing across different contexts. Precise instructions matter because agents fall back on familiar patterns when given vague directions, making skills a useful place to encode the context, trade-offs, intuition, and taste that individual prompts cannot reliably communicate.

design.title: Bioluminescent Alien Worlds That Will Make You Want to Pack Your Bags for the Cosmos
design.summary: Vancouver-based 3D artist Calder Moore builds bioluminescent forests, glowing flora, towering monoliths, and surreal planetary systems under twilight or starry skies.

design.title: This 3D Artist Achieves Incredible Realism to Breathe Life into Striking Character Designs
design.summary: A smug goblin, an albino demon, an adolescent chimp, and a dark elf showcase the striking realism of Australian 3D artist Tom Newbury.

marketing.title: Abandoned carts aren't just an email opportunity
marketing.summary: SimpliSafe uses abandoned-cart activity and other digital signals to trigger direct mail within Braze-powered customer journeys. It matches up to 90% of digital leads and prospects to physical addresses. L'Occitane brings purchase history into the mix, dynamically tailoring mail creative to customers' interests. Both are winners of Lob's 2026 Postmark Awards , highlighting what modern, data-driven direct mail can look like. See the campaigns and get a practical checklist of tactics behind this year's winners. Explore the winners and get the checklist

marketing.title: Google AI Mode sends 57% of product links to Google Shopping
marketing.summary: Google's AI search experience keeps shoppers within its own ecosystem, especially for fashion and beauty products. A study of 55,198 AI answers found that 57% of product links led to Google Shopping and 46.5% of US product answers linked only to Google pages. Brands may gain visibility in AI search without receiving website traffic.

marketing.title: What marketers should know about the legal risks of algorithmic pricing
marketing.summary: Dynamic pricing, where every customer sees the same demand-driven price, is relatively safe, but pricing that changes based on the shopper carries much greater legal risk. A promo code sent to one segment or a retargeted offer that undercuts the public price can count as personalized pricing. Dozens of bills are pending across more than 20 states, and the FTC has drafted a policy statement on when the practice is misleading or unfair. False-advertising laws also apply, since a sale price only some shoppers see may misrepresent the discount.

marketing.title: Drive more app downloads for $0
marketing.summary: Turn high-engagement UGC comments into app downloads by replying to questions about problems your app solves. Read the comment on camera, answer it, show the relevant app feature, then tell viewers where to download it. One family meal-planning app used this tactic to generate 100K+ views on a reply to a post with 8M+ views and 16K comments.

marketing.title: How to Implement & Measure Viral Loops: Stories from SaaS Growth Experts
marketing.summary: The most sustainable viral loops in SaaS come from invites the product already requires, not from asking users to refer someone. A QR code generator labels every free code so each real-world scan exposes the brand, while an assessment tool reaches new users whenever a recruiter invites a candidate. K-factor sums every loop into one growth rate, and the useful inputs are invite-accept rate and invitee activation rather than opens or clicks. Gating rewards on activation and fixing activation first keep the loop fueled, since users who never reach value have nothing to share.

marketing.title: Instagram just launched long-form video…but I don't think brands should use it
marketing.summary: Instagram's new long-form video format isn't a priority for brands that haven't mastered short-form content. Brands should first create Reels over 60 seconds that earn strong watch time and engagement, then turn successful formats into consistent series that build an audience. Long-form is worth exploring only when short videos can persuade viewers to watch more. Create content that builds brand influence and drives action, not just views.

marketing.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
marketing.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach marketers, growth leaders and brand teams where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

marketing.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it's shifting to a logged-in experience
marketing.summary: Reddit is shifting toward a primarily logged-in experience as AI-powered search reduces traffic from Google and other search engines. The move aims to limit AI scraping and encourage data-licensing deals while giving Reddit more user data to personalize feeds and target ads. Search referrals fell by more than 1M per week in October, while daily active users in the US dropped 2% year over year to 50.7M. Reddit will test the change in select markets outside the US in Q4.

marketing.title: B2B Events: What to Start, Stop, and Scale in 2027 (Webinar)
marketing.summary: 9 B2B marketers share what worked and failed at their 2026 events and what they'll change in 2027. They'll cover booth design, meeting bookings, and success metrics. In a blitz format, speakers get 2 minutes to make their case before the audience votes on finalists, who get 4 minutes to elaborate. This event will take place today at 12 PM ET.

marketing.title: The horror movie marketing hall of fame
marketing.summary: Horror campaigns have to hook audiences without giving the scare away, usually on small budgets. The Blair Witch Project and Longlegs built worlds with fake websites and real-world touchpoints that turned curiosity into word of mouth. Backrooms tapped a fandom that already existed online rather than starting from scratch. Smile planted actors with creepy grins at sports broadcasts and earned about 170 million trackable impressions without buying airtime. Obsession made its villain feel real with a text-me billboard and her own Letterboxd account, turning a $750K budget into $522M worldwide.

marketing.title: How Brands Make Boring Industries Desirable
marketing.summary: Categories where shoppers once bought whatever was cheapest or on the shelf leave more room for a brand to change how the whole category feels. Jolie positions its filtered showerhead against skincare rather than plumbing, while Scrub Daddy's smiling face doubles as the sponge's grip and its social personality. Making a commodity feel premium, designing it to be left out, or turning its use into a ritual gives buyers a reason to care which brand they pick in a category where that choice barely mattered.

marketing.title: The best CMOs think like CFOs
marketing.summary: CMOs should use incrementality tests to identify which marketing channels drive growth and deserve more budget.

marketing.title: Buyers type the category
marketing.summary: 61% of B2B buyers start AI vendor research with broad category questions, while 18% search for alternatives to tools they already use.

marketing.title: Short-form audiences are rented attention
marketing.summary: Brands are prioritizing deeper audience relationships over views and follower counts through long-form content and smaller creators.

founders.title: Stop vibe coding. Start shipping.
founders.summary: Kiro turns your prompts into specs, designs, and tested code — not just prototypes. Spec-driven development means your AI-generated code actually makes it to production. Early-stage to Series A startups: get up to 1 year of Kiro Pro+ free. Terms and Conditions apply, linked HERE.

founders.title: The Old B2B Pricing Model Is Dead. These Are the New Kings
founders.summary: AI will fundamentally alter software pricing. Seat-based pricing, the traditional B2B pricing model, is slowly fading away. New B2B pricing models charge for work done. This post looks at three emerging pricing models that look promising.

founders.title: Keith Rabois' New Rules of Vertical AI
founders.summary: Frontier models will continue to improve. Vertical AI that does the job end-to-end gains from improving models. Use model routing to optimize workflows - long term, model mixes and open-weights can recapture margin. Let labs supply intelligence, but own the data loops, private data, corner cases, and last-mile liability. Earn data by having a primary product that customers pay for, and learn what labs can't by doing work previously done by humans.

founders.title: Nobody Learns in the Clean Half
founders.summary: AI is taking over the routine work that used to teach new hires their job, like reconciling ledgers or fixing small bugs. ATMs took over cash handling and left bank tellers with customer problems and loan conversations. The worry is who learns the messy half now, since a 500-person compliance team might shrink to 30 and the cuts land on people who learned on the easy tasks. One startup studio hired its AI engineer by asking them to fix a real SEO problem and demo the fix, so new hires hit judgment calls in their first months.

founders.title: Inside PM at Anthropic: Who Makes It, and Who Doesn't
founders.summary: A bigger title at a bigger company counts for less than it used to when Anthropic hires product managers. The head of product for Anthropic's research teams walks through how she hires and ramps PMs on the team that incubated Claude Code. Her favorite candidate is a startup's first PM who also did customer success and business development, since people who've worked without structure go find answers themselves. The team also dropped annual planning for one-month plans, because yearly OKRs went out of date within two weeks.

founders.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
founders.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach founders, operators and startup leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

founders.title: Introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway
founders.summary: Vercel's AI Gateway now lets teams point an app at a virtual model ID such as vmc/coding-agent, after 125 new models from more than 10 labs landed on the gateway in 90 days. The company says the underlying model, fallbacks, and data-retention settings can be swapped without a redeploy.

founders.title: You can now generate, preview, and edit documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, and more directly in Gemini
founders.summary: Gemini users can now generate, preview, and edit files right inside chat. PDF preview and edits are supported on both the web and mobile, while all other formats are supported on the web only. The capability is available to all users in all languages where the Gemini app is available.

founders.title: Introducing Mintlify Base
founders.summary: Mintlify Base is a workspace where people and agents work from the same specs, runbooks, and onboarding pages. It can help draft, develop, and refine pages. Teammates can contribute to the work or hand the work to an agent. Agents can follow style guides, review checklists, and page templates. Base has a built-in MCP server that other agents can read from.

founders.title: Persistence Is a Numbers Game: 150 Startups, One Collapse, and the One That Worked
founders.summary: Startup studios look like a machine for making companies until the studio itself runs out of money. A former studio CTO who helped build more than 150 startups walks through why theirs collapsed. It carried 50 staff on a model where partners had to fund every accelerator round, so when the partners slowed down, the payroll didn't. The CTO lost their stake in the collapse, and their next company runs with a skeleton crew.

founders.title: What one person can actually operate
founders.summary: Stelae is a small hosting service run by one person. Most of the technical decisions made stem from the fact that there is no team, no on-call rotation, and nobody to escalate to. The system assumes nobody will be there when something breaks, and tries to be boring enough for that to be fine. This post discusses what that looks like in the code.

founders.title: A good FDE engagement is one that's designed to end
founders.summary: Forward Deployed Engineers should aim to leave customers able to build their own agents.

founders.title: We Told A Founder To Shut His Company Down And Take Our Money With It
founders.summary: Hustle Fund told a portfolio founder to shut his company down, and says his early, honest updates are why he'd get another check.

founders.title: How the Same 16,000 Users Behave in AI Search vs. Google
founders.summary: Traditional Google search behavior is a poor predictor of AI Search behavior.

founders.title: The Sane Asylum
founders.summary: There has never been a better time in history to build a highly profitable business with significant scale without raising or hiring a ton.

crypto.title: Utah files criminal charges against Kalshi and executives
crypto.summary: Utah's attorney general charged Kalshi, CEO Tarek Mansour, and COO Luana Lopes Lara with promoting illegal online gambling, including letting an undercover agent place wagers. It follows the state's civil suit on October 20. The CFTC sued Utah on Tuesday to block enforcement against prediction markets, and has sued at least 10 states. Kalshi's own February suit against Utah failed when a judge ruled federal law didn't preempt state enforcement.

crypto.title: Tokenized GOOGL Drops Nearly 12% Alongside After-Hours Stock Selloff
crypto.summary: Tokenized GOOGL fell nearly 12% on-chain as Alphabet shares sold off after earnings, with a Uniswap pool processing roughly $603,000 in volume over five minutes during the repricing. The near-instantaneous price adjustment shows that on-chain tokenized equity pools can track TradFi price events in real time, without waiting for the next trading session. The $603,000 in five-minute Uniswap volume also reveals the depth constraints of current tokenized equity infrastructure, where thin liquidity amplifies price swings relative to the underlying stock's exchange order book.

crypto.title: OKXICE Objections Rise to 33 as Stock-Token Lineup Shrinks
crypto.summary: OKX's tokenized equities venue OKXICE (xStocks) has received 33 issuer objections covering 31 of its 63 originally proposed symbols, leaving only 32 symbols without a disclosed objection ahead of launch. Public company issuers are opposing the listing of their equity without explicit consent, forcing OKX to trim the tradable universe before trading opens. The attrition exposes the consent gap RWA stock-token platforms face when listing securities without formal issuer authorization, a friction that could constrain the tokenized equities market to willing issuers rather than the full public-equity universe.

crypto.title: VanEck launches diversified ETF combining stocks, bonds and Bitcoin
crypto.summary: VanEck listed the Wealth Builder ETF (NYSE: WBMO), an actively managed fund-of-funds blending stocks, bonds, gold, and real assets with a 2% Bitcoin target (1%-5% permitted range), on NYSE, with BTC exposure routed through a spot Bitcoin ETP rather than direct coin holdings. The product converts VanEck's existing adviser-only Wealth Builder model portfolios into a publicly tradeable wrapper, with VanEck retaining discretion over allocations and rebalancing. VanEck positions Bitcoin as a scarce, non-sovereign complement to gold for purchasing-power protection, drawing on a $244.1 billion AUM base as of September 30. The launch continues a distribution push that began in March, when VanEck partnered with retirement platform Basic Capital to offer its digital asset ETPs inside US employer 401(k) plans.

crypto.title: Ethena Pay's 12% Earn+: what's behind the yield
crypto.summary: Ethena Pay is only the interface, and funds move to an Upshift vault curated by Steakhouse. The strategy supplies USDe on Aave V4 on Avalanche, borrows USDT, swaps to more USDe, and repeats, at about 11x leverage. Base USDe supply yield is about 0%, so the 12% comes almost entirely from Merkl incentives and would be deeply negative without them. Risks include liquidation if USDe or USDT dislocate (USDe briefly hit about $0.65 on Binance in Oct. 2025), incentives ending or diluting, and smart contract risk.

crypto.title: More Americans Have Tried Crypto, But Few Are Sticking With It
crypto.summary: A survey of 1,545 US adults, commissioned by the DeFi Education Fund, shows lifetime crypto ownership rising to 22% from 18%, yet active past-year usage held flat at 13%, pointing to a retention problem more than an awareness gap. The lifetime figure grew because lapsed users returned: among respondents who had not used crypto in the past year, 11% reported prior ownership, up from 5% a year ago, while new-user entry did not accelerate. Trust in crypto exchanges (4% high trust) and decentralized platforms (5%) sits far below the 42-48% high-trust ratings earned by banks and credit unions, and DeFi familiarity registers at just 2% "very familiar." Despite the GENIUS Act establishing federal stablecoin rules, stated interest in learning about stablecoins fell to 7% from 11%, and DeFi interest dropped to 8% from 11%, showing that regulatory clarity has not translated into consumer engagement.

crypto.title: Bitcoin dips below $80,000 as Samsung-led tech jitters and a hawkish Fed weigh on crypto
crypto.summary: Bitcoin fell from $81,700 to $79,800 during Thursday's Asian session after Samsung shares dropped over 5% on a chip-division profit miss (106.5 trillion won versus 108.5 trillion won expected), pulling the Kospi down 2% and Nasdaq futures down 1.4%. The Federal Reserve's hawkish hold at 3.75-4% added pressure, with Chair Kevin Warsh citing persistent inflation and ING forecasting a December rate hike following September's increase. $356 million in crypto futures liquidated over 24 hours, including $205 million from long positions, with BTC futures accounting for $94 million and ETH for $72 million. Elevated real yields reduce the speculative capital pool, and a December Fed hike would tighten that constraint into year-end.

crypto.title: What you need to spend for crypto cards to pay for themselves
crypto.summary: This post compares six paid crypto card tiers against their free versions to find the monthly spend needed to cover the annual fee. The cheapest are MetaMask Metal ($199 a year, break-even $829 a month, 3% vs 1% cashback capped at $10K a year) and Plasma One Core ($199, $900 a month, with rewards paid in XPL). In the middle are ether.fi Luxe ($199, $2,829 a month), ether.fi Pinnacle ($999, $5,530 a month) and KAST Premium ($1,000, $5,667 a month). The extreme case is KAST Private at $10,000 a year, which needs $28,778 a month, or over $345K a year in card spending. KAST cashback can't be withdrawn and may expire, and ether.fi and Plasma pay in tokens (ETHFI and XPL), so token prices change your real return.

crypto.title: Card revenue is 63% of ether.fi's revenue
crypto.summary: Card revenue is 63% of ether.fi's revenue, up from about 15% a year ago.

crypto.title: SoFi Reports $161.6 Million in Q3 Crypto Revenue, $1.6 Million Net
crypto.summary: SoFi posted $161.6 million in gross Q3 crypto revenue, retaining only $1.6 million net after costs, equal to 0.3% of the bank's financial-services segment revenue.

crypto.title: Allium, blockchain data provider, discloses security breach
crypto.summary: Allium detected unauthorized access to some systems on October 25, notified affected customers, and hired an independent cybersecurity firm.

crypto.title: Pendle cut liquidity incentives by more than half in Q3, and TVL still grew

it.title: Serval triples valuation to $3 billion as businesses adopt AI workflow automation
it.summary: Serval raised $150 million in a Sequoia-led round at a $3 billion valuation, tripling its valuation since December. The company builds AI agents for IT operations, including employee access management, troubleshooting, and software and hardware asset management. Serval positions its platform as an alternative to established IT service management products such as ServiceNow, with permissions and approvals controlled by IT and security teams.

it.title: Oracle wants to bill you for every AI task, not just every seat
it.summary: Oracle plans to introduce usage-based AI charges alongside existing subscriptions for its Fusion enterprise applications. Customers will consume AI units as automated tasks are completed, allowing Oracle to grow revenue without adding user licenses. The approach reflects a broader shift in enterprise software pricing from per-seat subscriptions toward charging for automated work, introducing new considerations for software budgets and cost forecasting.

it.title: The hidden cost of AI is now governance
it.summary: As artificial intelligence projects transition from pilots to production, governance has emerged as a significant hidden cost spanning IT, security, legal, risk, and data teams. Retrofitting controls late in the process can add months of project delays and double expected costs, making risk-tiered governance and early automation essential for scalable enterprise AI adoption.

it.title: IT skills shortage often a complexity problem in disguise
it.summary: Some enterprise IT staffing challenges stem from unnecessarily complex systems rather than a lack of qualified candidates. Years of customizations, undocumented dependencies, and fragmented architectures create environments that require highly specialized knowledge. Simplify infrastructure, document dependencies, and reduce technical debt before assuming additional hiring or training will solve the problem.

it.title: When your AI vendor goes belly up
it.summary: As enterprises adopt products from a growing number of AI startups, CIOs face the possibility that some vendors will shut down, be acquired, or change their business models. Unlike conventional software replacements, losing an AI provider can introduce complications involving proprietary models, workflow dependencies, and customer data. This article examines how organizations can prepare exit strategies, preserve data access, and reduce their dependence on individual providers.

it.title: Workbrew: secure the open source running your company
it.summary: One install is all it takes for a Homebrew package, npm module, editor extension, or app to land on a Mac with zero review. Workbrew shows you all the software installed across your fleet, flags the vulnerable packages, and lets you upgrade or remove them in one click. Try it for free , with no device or user limits.

it.title: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work
it.summary: Microsoft is making the GitHub-developed Copilot harness available through Microsoft Foundry, providing developers and enterprise customers with a managed multi-model orchestration layer. The harness powers various Copilot experiences and supports over twenty frontier models, open standards, and tools while routing work intelligently based on tasks. Recently ported to Rust for improved performance, the system manages the agent loop, sandbox, governance, and optimization.

it.title: Slackbot gets more proactive, in more places
it.summary: Slack introduced event-triggered Slackbot tasks that can respond to messages, reactions, list updates, and channel creation events. The update also includes Slackbot Mini, a desktop interface for accessing the assistant outside Slack, and expanded Skills capabilities for sharing reusable workflows across teams. Administrators and users can configure approval requirements for automated actions, extending Slackbot beyond conversational assistance into workflow execution.

it.title: AWS Lambda durable functions now exports live telemetry for execution insights
it.summary: AWS Lambda has announced the Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter plugin, which captures step-by-step histories of durable executions and exports them to 13 built-in destinations like Amazon S3 and CloudWatch. Alongside the plugin, AWS released a companion Model Context Protocol server that allows AI agents to query the telemetry data using natural language. The exporter is available at no additional charge across regions supporting Lambda durable functions for TypeScript, Python, Java, and Go.

it.title: Apple unveils groundbreaking MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and Touch for the first time on Mac
it.summary: Apple introduced its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, featuring a tandem OLED display, M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and up to 24 hours of battery life. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch models, the laptops also include Wi-Fi 7, Thunderbolt 5, and up to 16TB of storage. Prices start at $2,899, with availability beginning November 6. The launch adds another premium option for enterprise Mac fleets and specialized professional workloads.

it.title: Chinese AI invasion gives enterprises a new way to control cost
it.summary: Enterprises are increasingly adopting affordable Chinese open-weight AI models to reduce soaring token spending on US proprietary frontier models. While some companies face integration hurdles, infrastructure limitations, and geopolitical concerns that prompt hesitation, organizations like Red Hat are successfully utilizing these models to control costs by allocating workloads between proprietary and open-weight alternatives.

it.title: Granola crunches up a dictation feature to compete with Wispr
it.summary: AI meeting-notes app Granola introduced a free dictation feature that allows Mac users to speak and automatically convert their words into formatted text across applications. The company plans to bring the capability to Windows and iOS. The move follows Wispr's expansion into meeting transcription, illustrating how voice productivity tools are converging around similar capabilities.

it.title: GitHub powering up four million extra cores to stop its service going down
it.summary: GitHub reported 7.4 billion code commits in September, five times the volume from a year earlier, driven partly by AI coding agents.

it.title: Systemd adds support for Rust
it.summary: The Linux system and service manager systemd is adding support for components written in Rust.

it.title: Cisco IT's Endpoint Observability Strategy
it.summary: Cisco IT reduced its endpoint telemetry data volume by 75% while improving troubleshooting and digital resilience by implementing a right-sized telemetry model in Splunk Observability Cloud.

hardware.title: Apple's tandem OLED MacBook Pro adds an in-panel touch sensor, 2,000 nits, and a 3-pound 14-inch
hardware.summary: Apple's new 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro uses a tandem OLED panel rated at 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and 10 to 120Hz refresh, with the touch sensor built into the panel rather than layered on top. It drops to 3 and 4 pounds, adds a Dynamic Island, and runs M5 Pro or M5 Max with up to 128GB of memory. Pricing starts at $2,899, shipping November 6.

hardware.title: PsiQuantum shows an 8×8 optical circuit switch with 1.2 dB loss for AI data center networks
hardware.summary: PsiQuantum unveiled an 8×8 optical circuit switch built on the silicon photonics platform it developed for quantum computing, measuring typical insertion loss of 1.2 dB, 40 dB crosstalk, and under 3 ms reconfiguration without amplification. Samples are going to select customers, with commercial products promised in the coming months. A 64×64 barium titanate switch used in its quantum systems isn't needed for this first version but offers a path to faster future parts.

hardware.title: Altera's Agilex 2X FPGAs claim 1.8x performance per watt, with 256 Gbps transceivers and PCIe 7.0
hardware.summary: Altera announced Agilex 2X, four FPGA families spanning high-end to I/O-centric parts, led by Agilex 27 with a third-generation HyperFlex fabric claiming 1.8x performance per watt over Agilex 7. It adds a chip-wide HyperFlow data network, transceivers up to 256 Gbps, hardened 800GbE and 1.6TbE, PCIe 6.0 and 7.0, LPDDR6, UCIe, and post-quantum-ready secure boot. Quartus support starts in mid-November, with engineering samples in the second half of 2027.

hardware.title: Eclypsium shows AI model weights can be altered in memory after integrity checks pass
hardware.summary: Eclypsium demonstrated changing a model's weights in memory after integrity checks pass, so the model file, container, hash, and signatures on disk all stay valid. Attack paths run through host firmware, management controllers, and DPUs, and the report says Nvidia, AMD, Intel, and Arm systems are all exposed. Its fix is DPUs that enforce security policy independently of the AI system, plus full component inventories.

hardware.title: MIT's snake-inspired soft robot crawls the small intestine using kirigami traction sleeves
hardware.summary: MIT built a tethered soft enteroscope to cover the small intestine, a 20- to 25-foot tube that double balloon enteroscopy currently covers slowly by hand. Four-chamber inflatable actuators bend and extend the body, anchoring balloons at the head and tail take turns gripping, and kirigami sleeves pop out needles for traction. In animal tests, it advanced about 6.5 feet and used its camera, drug sprayer, and biopsy clips.

hardware.title: Seoul Biosys Begins Production of Rare Earth-Free White Micro LEDs
hardware.summary: Seoul Biosys has started producing rare earth-free white micro LEDs using WICOP technology, which eliminates the need for traditional packaging. The new LEDs measure 25µm x 10µm and achieve 0.015 lumens, with plans to double light efficiency to 200 lumens per watt. This innovation aims to reduce manufacturing costs and environmental impact, targeting applications in smart glasses, AR displays, and AI data transmission.

hardware.title: Marvell is reportedly in advanced talks to buy laser maker Lumentum at a roughly $91B valuation
hardware.summary: Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum, which makes the lasers and optical modules that move data between AI servers, with an announcement possible as soon as next week. Lumentum rose about 11% after hours to a roughly $91 billion valuation, while Marvell fell more than 8%. Marvell held only about $3.9 billion in cash last quarter. Neither company has confirmed the talks.

hardware.title: SpaceX no longer needs NASA, and NASA's leverage is shrinking as a result
hardware.summary: SpaceX no longer depends on NASA contracts to survive, while NASA depends heavily on SpaceX's rockets and capsules, which cuts the agency's negotiating leverage. SpaceX told NASA it will stop flying Crew Dragon by or before 2030 and has stopped selling commercial Falcon 9 launches for missions after 2028. That would leave NASA's ISS crew transport and station deorbit plans exposed.

hardware.title: Intel trials open robotics architecture with SAP in Chinese demo
hardware.summary: Intel, in partnership with SAP, tested an open robotics architecture at its Chengdu site, integrating SAP's Warehouse Management with AI and autonomous mobile robots.

hardware.title: Palmer Luckey on why ceiling fans broke inside-out VR tracking and how Oculus secured its screens
hardware.summary: Inside-out tracking took years to survive real rooms, where glass, reflections, moving people, curtains, and ceiling fans break the scene model.

hardware.title: XREAL AURA launches as the first wired Android XR glasses, with a 70-degree field of view
hardware.summary: Google and XREAL launched AURA, transparent-lens glasses that run Android XR and project apps across a 70-degree view.

hardware.title: DOJ reportedly questions Nvidia's $12.9B Hugging Face deal over control of open-model distribution
hardware.summary: Reuters reports the DOJ is questioning whether owning the main distribution hub for open models would let Nvidia disadvantage rival chip and AI companies or gain leverage in negotiations.

hardware.title: FuriosaAI raises $620M at a $2.9B valuation to scale its 180 W RNGD inference chip
hardware.summary: FuriosaAI raised $620 million at a $2.9 billion valuation, about four times its prior round, to scale its RNGD inference chip, a 180 W part it claims matches GPU throughput at half the power or less.
